An re- exploration of James' psyche as it is reflected through the very essence of Silent Hill. His descent into trauma, grief, guilt, repression and derealization is tragically heartbreaking as you follow him through the depths of a purgatory of his own making. Truth, and its discovery, are often a terrifying thing.

A psychological horror masterpiece.

When I first saw this game get unveiled, along with the trailers and the companies behind it, I though that this remake was going to be a absolute trainwreck. Instead however, we got a remake of a beloved classic that is damn near perfect.

Everything that made the original Silent hill 2 so good is still present here, alongside MANY improvements that make this experience better than the original!

The combat is some of the best i've seen in a horror game, the boss fights are significantly improved from the original, the puzzles are really good (even if they can be really cryptic and confusing at time), the extra events and story beats are amazing and dont drag things down too much, and the survival horror elements at play here are way better and more prominent than they were in the original.

My only major gripe with the remake is that the game was very laggy and stuttery at some points, with massive frame drops happening though out my game (Idk if this was because of my hardware or if the game isn't optimized the best, but i've seen others have similar issues, even on machines way more powerful than mine)

Overall, if you are a big fan of Silent hill, or horror stuff in general, and your pc is up to the task, this is a game i'd recommend grabbing!

All of this, combined with the story and wonderful characters, gave me an unforgettable experience that I thoroughly enjoyed from start to finish.

This masterpiece is worth every penny. Bravo! This is how remakes should be made.

The game also features an incredible soundtrack that can truly touch your soul and stay with you long after you hear it. Silent Hill 2 Remake deserves all the huge success it has received.

-The map exploration and puzzles are great there was 1 or 2 puzzles that were just dumb or maybe im just dumb probably both, this game actually rewards you (most) of the time for exploring, atmosphere is fantastic and graphics are even better constantly creating eerie vibes and stunning views but i was locked at 60fps for whatever reason.

-Combat was a hard learning curve (hardest difficulty) basic enemy's felt like a dark souls boss and got even harder with new enemy's introduced with that being said the enemy's are very well made and you can learn there attack patterns, once you understand it combat is peak and you can solo the entire game with a wooden plank elden ring style.

-Story is one of my favorite of all time as i related to alot of it and it had a deeper meaning to me but you also get to understand why each monster was created and what the town and its people are, alot of the story is up to you to determine there's tons of theory's of wtf is going on but honestly it makes the games story that much better leaving it up to you.

Overall i highly recommend this game especially if you like Resident Evil.

James walks the fog like a penitent carrying his own coffin. Mary’s letter is the noose; the town tightens it. Pyramid Head is not a monster—he is the verdict you wrote before you arrived. Every corridor a confessional, every mannequin a mirror that learned to hate you.

Combat is clumsy grace, survival-horror liturgy: swing, bleed, pray the bullets last. Puzzles are occult riddles carved into flesh and rust. The remake polishes the blade without dulling the guilt—Bloober knelt at the altar and did not flinch. Multiple endings wait like hanging judges.

Atmosphere so thick it clots the lungs. Sound design that whispers your sins back at you. A masterpiece of wretched beauty.

The fog knows your name. Enter anyway.

I think this game is one of those games that really linger and stay with you after you've played them.

I adored it and would absolutely play it again.

This is a remake of one of the most influential psychological horror games.

Bloober Team nailed the atmosphere in this remake.
It looks great, sounds great, and they, in my opinion, upgraded the combat system.
Akira Yamaoka produced one of the best video game soundtracks and it perfectly fits the moody melancholic vibe of the game.
On hard combat difficulty, the game is quite challenging.
Enemies hit really hard and healing items and ammo are limited, so you can’t just button mash or shoot your way through the game.
Hard puzzle difficulty is surprisingly well balanced, though some hints in the game are very esoteric.
The performance on PC is pretty bad, it suffers from traversal stutter and random hitches.
It doesn’t completely ruin the game, but it is obvious, it needed more time in the oven for polish and optimization.

If you are a Survival Horror fan looking for a great story get this.

I bought the Silent Hill 2 remake specifically to play a game with great fall and Halloween atmosphere, and it does not disappoint—they absolutely nail the atmosphere. The story and characters are engaging and incredibly well-done, and the combat feels solid and well-designed for a horror title.

If you have the hardware, this is an amazing remake. The graphics are a real treat on an RTX 4090, running smoothly and letting the atmosphere shine through.

However, be warned about playing this on handhelds. I could not get it to run acceptably on my Steam Deck, and the experience on an ROG Ally X was terrible. Unreal Engine 5 currently runs broken on those Windows handhelds; key visual components like volumetric lighting are way off, and the crucial fog effect is completely gone. Without the fog, the core atmosphere is ruined, making it an unenjoyable experience at all.

I am not a puzzle person, so I used help online for those sections, but it was well worth it just for the really engrossing story and the phenomenal atmosphere that the game delivers on high-end hardware.
